Target languages that require an explicit relative-clause object must keep the suffix tied to ٱلَّذِينَ, not to the later excluded groups.
Target language may miss that غَيْرِ excludes a contrasting class from the requested path rather than starting a new independent description.
Target language may over-read لَا as clausal negation or omit its reinforcement of the second excluded class.
Target languages should keep the second suffix attached to the passive-participle group, not to ٱلَّذِينَ in the preceding relative clause.
Target language may need an explicit subject for أَنْعَمْتَ, while Arabic marks only the same 2ms addressee active from 1:5-6.
Target language may be tempted to supply an explicit agent of غضب, but the Arabic passive participle leaves the agent unspoken.
